A code comment says an interrupted wait is not a failed read, so it must not count against anything; retry until the fd is ready or the wait fails.
Any other select error returns getCharError.
If the cancel pipe is readable the loop returns getCharCancelled, and if the tty fd is readable it reads the byte.
The select has a nil timeout, so an unbounded wait is expected, and a retry cap would make it give up with an error while the user simply hadn't pressed a key.

The 30-process cap is global: bgSemaphore is created as a channel with capacity maxBgProcesses at src/terminal.go:1178.
In dispatchAsync each goroutine takes t.bgSemaphore before running and releases it afterwards.
The 3-per-action cap is per action: one semaphore per action is created with capacity maxBgProcessesPerAction at src/terminal.go:5760.
A job must acquire the per-action semaphore before its goroutine starts.
When an action's 3 slots are full, every queued item except the last is called with item(false) and only the last is kept in bgQueue, so a burst of events keeps only the newest request per action.
The false argument to the callback presumably means skip rather than run.
The likely purpose is bounding resource use: the global cap limits total child processes and the per-action cap stops one frequently firing event like focus or every(1) from using all slots.
There is no benchmark or discussion text in the checkout; issues #4418 and #4419 are only referenced by number.

claims.text: In the cancellable path of getch(), unix.Select runs in a for loop; on EINTR the code continues retrying without a limit, and any other error returns getCharError.
A code comment says an interrupted wait is not a failed read, so it must not count against anything, and should retry until the fd is ready or the wait fails.
Commit 1578b7c3 ("Fix spurious exit while waiting for a key with --listen", fixes #4917) removed the retry limit on EINTR.
Before the fix, getch() charged EINTR against a 100-iteration limit meant for read attempts, and the count reset only after a byte was read.
Signals arriving during an idle prompt used up the 100 iterations; running out returned getCharError, which became Event{Fatal} and exit status 2.
SA_RESTART does not restart select(), so the cancellable path sees EINTR, while the non-cancellable blocking read is restarted and does not.
Therefore only the --listen path was affected.
waitReadable() already retries EINTR without a limit.
Select has no timeout (nil), so the loop exits only on cancel, a readable fd, or a non-EINTR error.

claims.text: res.clearCookie builds options as { path: '/', ...options, expires: new Date(1) }, deletes opts.maxAge, and calls this.cookie(name, '', opts).
Code comments say 'Force cookie expiration by setting expires to the past' and 'ensure maxAge is not passed'.

The intent is for clearCookie to always send a cookie that expires in the past so the client deletes it; the v4 changelog states 'clearCookie will set a cookie with an expires in the past to instruct clients to delete the cookie'.
res.cookie converts maxAge into a new expires of Date.now() + maxAge and replaces any expires already set.
If a caller's maxAge reached res.cookie, the cookie would get a future expiry and not be cleared, so deleting maxAge first prevents that.
The behavior was first deprecated in v4 by commit f42b160b, titled '[v4] Deprecate res.clearCookie accepting options.maxAge and options.expires (#5672)'.

claims.text: In getch the cancellable path is a for loop around unix.Select, and on EINTR it continues; the loop has no counter or retry limit.
Any other select error returns getCharError.
A code comment states an interrupted wait is not a failed read and must not count against anything; retry until fd is ready or the wait fails.
EINTR is treated as a spurious wakeup, not a failure.
The select has a nil timeout so it waits indefinitely, and the loop ends only when a cancel signal arrives on the pipe (getCharCancelled), the tty becomes readable, or a non-EINTR error occurs.
A retry cap could make a key read fail after enough unrelated signals even though nothing is wrong.
The EINTR check first appeared in commit 3f94bcb5bf, "Cancel key reading when 'execute' triggered via a server request (#4653)" (2026-01-09), at src/tui/light_unix.go:158.
At HEAD the same EINTR check also exists in waitReadable.
No design note, issue or comment beyond the code comment explains why there is no retry cap.

claims.text: The lock is taken at byte offset 4096 (_win_lock_offset = 4096), not byte 0.
Acquire seeks to the offset before msvcrt.locking(..., LK_NBLCK, 1), and release seeks to the same offset before LK_UNLCK.
Windows byte-range locks are mandatory, so locking offset 4096 lets external readers read the PID payload at byte 0 without PermissionError.
The lock file holds the owning PID plus a newline so external pollers can read it, and the PID is written at offset 0.

Commit e4a6f5098e ("fix(watch): serialize _rebuild_lock on Windows via msvcrt", closes #3881) gives the same reason: lock a byte range at offset 4096 so external readers can still read the PID at byte 0 without mandatory lock PermissionErrors.
That commit is the first to add msvcrt.locking to _rebuild_lock.
_try_skill_lock locks byte 0 (fh.seek(0)) in install.py.
The skill lock file is never deleted and is not described as holding a PID payload.

4096 is likely just an offset past the short PID line.
graphify/install.py's _try_skill_lock locks byte 0 by seeking to 0 before locking.
The install.py lock file doesn't appear to carry a PID payload.

claims.text: No comment or commit message explains why abortIndex is half of MaxInt8; the stated reason is unknown.
The comment at context.go:56 only says abortIndex is 'a typical value used in abort functions'.
abortIndex is math.MaxInt8 >> 1, which is 63.
The value was added as math.MaxInt8 / 2 in commit 8f3047814e.
Commit c7a28f85 ('use bit shift operation instead of division') changed the division to a shift, leaving the value unchanged.
Abort() sets c.index = abortIndex.
IsAborted() returns c.index >= abortIndex, so abort is a range check rather than an equality check.

If abortIndex were 127, the c.index++ in Next() would likely overflow to -128, satisfy the loop condition, and run handlers that should have been skipped; with 63 the increment gives 64, still above any normal chain length.
safeInt8 caps the handler count at math.MaxInt8.
Copy() sets cp.index = abortIndex, so a copied context reports as aborted and runs no handlers.

_try_skill_lock and _release_skill_lock in install.py seek to byte 0 before locking.

The Windows msvcrt locking in _rebuild_lock first appeared in commit e4a6f5098e, "fix(watch): serialize _rebuild_lock on Windows via msvcrt".
The 4096 offset was chosen because Windows rejects reads of a locked region, so locking byte 0 would block readers of the PID there.

The per-action limit is a buffered channel of size maxBgProcessesPerAction, created for each action.
dispatchAsync takes the per-action semaphore without blocking, then the goroutine waits on the global semaphore and releases both when it finishes.
